summary: This work introduces error-detectable (ED) universal control of bosonic modes using a higher-energy-level ancilla ($|g\rangle$, $|e\rangle$, $|f\rangle$) to detect and post-select against ancilla relaxation events, suppressing operational errors that limit QEC gains in binomial codes. Numerical simulations demonstrate universal gate fidelities exceeding 99.6% and peak QEC gains of $8.33\times$ beyond break-even, with analytical arguments establishing that gains beyond $10\times$ are achievable with state-of-the-art transmon qubits having $T_1 \sim 100$ µs.
motivation: Current bosonic QEC implementations achieve coherence improvements only $\sim 2\times$ the physical qubit because ancilla-induced operational errors ($\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}$), not intrinsic cavity loss, dominate the error budget according to $G_{\mathrm{break}} \sim \alpha^2 \alpha_W \epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}$.
method: Error detection is implemented by using the intermediate $|e\rangle$ state as a herald: two-photon drives on the ancilla create effective Hilbert-space rotations in the $\{|g\rangle, |f\rangle\}$ subspace, combined with dispersive coupling to the bosonic mode. Post-selection discards trajectories where the ancilla is measured in $|e\rangle$, reducing operational error to $\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}} < 0.4\%$ for all logical operations on binomial codes (code space $\{|0_L\rangle = (|0\rangle + |4\rangle)/\sqrt{2}, |1_L\rangle = |2\rangle\}$) with $\sim 95\%$ success probability.
result: For repeated ED QEC cycles at $\kappa = 1/(2\,\mathrm{ms})$ and $\chi_e/2\pi = 1$ MHz, $\chi_f/2\pi = 2$ MHz: ED-A QEC (ancilla-only post-selection) achieves $T_1 = 18.76$ ms versus $3.35$ ms for physical qubits ($5.60\times$ gain); ED-AB QEC (ancilla plus bosonic-mode post-selection) reaches infidelity ratio $8.33\times$ at $t = 2375$ µs. Analytic error budget shows critical ancilla lifetime $1/\kappa_e^C \approx 91$ µs for $1/\kappa = 2$ ms, with saturation gain $G_{\mathrm{break}}^{\mathrm{sat}} \approx 39$ limited by residual cavity loss during correction.
